rationale:
Split into four children. Steps 1–2 of the supplied proof just apply the hypotheses: AllardRectifiabilityTheorem (second conjunct) and then FirstRectifiabilityTheorem. They stay in the parent. The substance is two independent analytic facts that hold for every varifold or measure. One of them has two reusable ingredients that the supplied proof names explicitly. The children are:
(weight_blowup) Def. 8.1.1 tested with f(y,S) = g(y): t^{-n}∫g(t^{-1}(z−x))dμ_V → θ∫_T g dH^n.
(plane_ball_measure) H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n.
(tangent_density) HasTangentPlane V x T θ ⇒ HasDensity n μ_V x (ofReal θ). This is the step-3 cut-off squeeze, built from the first two.
(null_transfer) If μ is locally finite on an open U and Z ⊆ U is μ-null with positive upper n-density at each point, then Z is H^n-null. This is the step-4 argument: outer regularity of μ⌞(ball), then Simon Ch. 1 Thm 3.3.
The step-4 compact exhaustion is replaced by an equivalent countable cover of U by balls with compact closure in U. The threshold θ(x) ≥ 1/k is phrased as upper density ≥ 1/(k+1), which is the same thing at points of M by step 3.

3. The second half of (ii) is tangent_density N n U V x T (θ x).
4. For (iii), apply null_transfer with μ := V.weight, U (V.isOpen_domain), compact finiteness (V.weight_finite_on_compact) and Z ⊆ M ⊆ U (hrep.1). At x ∈ Z, tangent_density gives limsup = ofReal(θ x) by Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq, and this is > 0 by ENNReal.ofReal_pos and hTx.2.1.

subproblems.title: Weight blow-up limit at a tangent point (Def. 8.1.1 tested with f(y,S) = g(y))
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U (Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) (Grassmannian N n) and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ. This is Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1: x ∈ U, θ > 0, and ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ ∫ f dv(T) as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n), ℝ), where V_{x,t} = rescaledMeasure V x t and v(T) = planeVarifoldMeasure T. Then for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), t^{-n} ∫ g(t^{-1}(z − x)) dμ_V(z) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n as t → 0 within (0, ∞). Here μ_V = V.weight, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^N, and all integrals are Bochner integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z, g (t⁻¹ • (z - x)) ∂V.weight) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n]))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, first sentence (the test function f(z,S) := g(z)), together with Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1.
Notation: G := Grassmannian N n, a compact space (SimonGMT Grassmannian.instCompactSpace). μ_V := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst. For t > 0, V_{x,t} := rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal(t⁻¹^n) • V.measure.map φ_t, where φ_t(z,S) := (t⁻¹ • (z − x), S). v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T = (μHE[n].restrict T.plane).map ι_T, where ι_T(y) := (y, T).

1. Fix g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) and put f(z,S) := g(z) on ℝ^N × G. Then f = g ∘ Prod.fst is continuous. If (z,S) ∉ tsupport g × G, then z ∉ tsupport g, so f(z,S) = g(z) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). The set tsupport g × G is compact: tsupport g is compact because g has compact support, and G is a compact space. So f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro), and f defines an element of C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

2. Apply the third conjunct of HasTangentPlane V x T θ to this f. It gives: t ↦ ∫ f dV_{x,t} tends to θ · ∫ f dv(T) along 𝓝[>] 0.

3. Plane side. ι_T is continuous, hence measurable. f is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for every measure on ℝ^N × G. By change of variables for image measures (integral_map), ∫ f dv(T) = ∫ f(ι_T(y)) d(μHE[n].restrict T.plane)(y) = ∫_{T.plane} g(y) dH^n(y).

4. Rescaled side. Let t > 0.
(a) By integral_smul_measure, ∫ f d(c • m) = c.toReal · ∫ f dm with c := ofReal(t⁻¹^n). Here c.toReal = t⁻¹^n because t⁻¹^n ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).
(b) φ_t is continuous, hence measurable. By integral_map, ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ_t) = ∫ f(φ_t(z,S)) dV.measure(z,S) = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dV.measure(z,S).
(c) The function y ↦ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) is continuous, and μ_V = V.measure.map Prod.fst with Prod.fst measurable. By integral_map, ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) dμ_V(y) = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dV.measure(z,S).
Combining (a)–(c): ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t⁻¹^n · ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) dμ_V(y) for every t > 0. No integrability hypothesis is needed, because integral_map and integral_smul_measure use only the measurability above.

5. The two functions of t in step 4 agree on (0, ∞), which belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Rewrite the limit of step 2 using step 3, then transfer it along this eventual equality (Tendsto.congr'). This gives t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (y − x)) dμ_V(y) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, which is the claim. ∎

HasTangentPlane applied to f gives ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ ∫ f dv(T) along 𝓝[>] 0.

subproblems.title: H^n of a closed disc in an n-plane: H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n
subproblems.statement: For N, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ G(N,n) (Grassmannian N n) and r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0: μHE[n](T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n, i.e. H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n. Here H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n
proof_key_steps: T.plane ∩ B_r(0) is the image of the closed r-ball of the n-dimensional inner product space P = T.plane under the isometric inclusion.
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] together with μHE[finrank P] = volume_P.
Haar scaling: volume_P(B_r(0)) = ofReal(r^n) · volume_P(ball 0 1).
A linear isometry P ≃ ℝ^n carries volume_P(ball 0 1) to ω_n = unitBallVolume n; ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(r)^n.

subproblems.title: A tangent plane of multiplicity θ at x forces Θ^n(μ_V, x) = θ
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U (Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1). Then the n-dimensional density of μ_V = V.weight at x exists and equals θ: densityRatio n μ_V x ρ = μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → ofReal θ as ρ → 0 within (0, ∞), with B_ρ(x) the closed ball and ω_n = unitBallVolume n. That is, HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal θ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal θ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Def. 8.1.1 tested with radial cut-offs). It uses two sibling results:
- (A) weight_blowup = Submission.intcpt_canon_weight_blowup_tendsto: for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ_V(z) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0;
- (B) plane_ball_measure = Submission.intcpt_canon_plane_closedBall_hausdorff: μHE[n](T.plane ∩ B_r(0)) = ω · ofReal(r)^n for r ≥ 0.
Notation: μ_V := V.weight; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; ω := unitBallVolume n; w := ω.toReal; b(t) := t⁻¹^n · μ_V(B_t(x)).toReal for t ∈ ℝ. All integrals are Bochner integrals.

0. ω ∈ (0, ∞). ω is the volume of the open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). volume is an additive Haar measure, so it is positive on nonempty open sets (measure_ball_pos) and finite on balls of this proper space (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence w > 0 and ω = ofReal w.

1. HasTangentPlane V x T θ gives x ∈ U and θ > 0. U is open (V.isOpen_domain), so ball x r ⊆ U for some r > 0. Put δ := r/2 > 0; then B_δ(x) ⊆ U. B_δ(x) is compact, so μ_V(B_δ(x)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact). Also, for t > 0 and z ∈ ℝ^N, ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ = t⁻¹ · dist(z, x).

2. Cut-offs. For real a < c define χ_{a,c}(y) := min(1, max(0, (c − ‖y‖)/(c − a))) for y ∈ ℝ^N. Its properties:
- χ_{a,c} is continuous and 0 ≤ χ_{a,c} ≤ 1.
- χ_{a,c}(y) = 1 when ‖y‖ ≤ a, since then (c − ‖y‖)/(c − a) ≥ 1.
- χ_{a,c}(y) = 0 when ‖y‖ ≥ c, since then (c − ‖y‖)/(c − a) ≤ 0.
So χ_{a,c} vanishes outside the compact set B_c(0), and χ_{a,c} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).

3. Integrability facts.
(a) Let a < c, t > 0 and t·c ≤ δ. Then z ↦ χ_{a,c}(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) is μ_V-integrable. It is continuous, so a.e.-strongly measurable. It is bounded in absolute value by the indicator 1_{B_δ(x)}: for z ∉ B_δ(x), ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ = t⁻¹ dist(z,x) > t⁻¹ δ ≥ c, so its value is 0. And 1_{B_δ(x)} is μ_V-integrable since μ_V(B_δ(x)) < ∞ (Integrable.mono').
(b) Let t ≤ δ. Then 1_{B_t(x)} is μ_V-integrable, since μ_V(B_t(x)) ≤ μ_V(B_δ(x)) < ∞. Also ∫ 1_{B_t(x)} dμ_V = μ_V(B_t(x)).toReal (integral_indicator_const, measureReal_def).
(c) Let r ≥ 0 and write H^n⌞T.plane := μHE[n].restrict T.plane. Then 1_{B_r(0)} is H^n⌞T.plane-integrable, and ∫_{T.plane} 1_{B_r(0)} dH^n = (μHE[n](B_r(0) ∩ T.plane)).toReal = (ω · ofReal(r)^n).toReal = w · r^n. This uses Measure.restrict_apply and (B); the value is finite because ω < ∞.
(d) Let a < c with c ≥ 0. Then χ_{a,c} is H^n⌞T.plane-integrable, being continuous and bounded in absolute value by 1_{B_c(0)} (use (c)).

4. Lower bound. Let 0 < κ < 1 and a ∈ ℝ with a < θ w κ^n. Put g⁻ := χ_{κ,1} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).
- Pointwise 1_{B_κ(0)} ≤ g⁻, since g⁻ = 1 on B_κ(0) and g⁻ ≥ 0. By monotonicity of the integral with 3(c),(d), I⁻ := ∫_{T.plane} g⁻ dH^n ≥ w κ^n. Since θ > 0, θ I⁻ ≥ θ w κ^n > a.
- By (A) applied to g⁻, t⁻¹^n ∫ g⁻(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ_V(z) → θ I⁻ along 𝓝[>] 0. So this quantity is eventually > a.
- Take 0 < t < κδ; this interval belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, and t·1 ≤ δ. For every z, g⁻(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(z): if z ∈ B_t(x) use g⁻ ≤ 1; otherwise ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ = t⁻¹ dist(z,x) > 1, so g⁻(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) = 0.
- By 3(a),(b) and integral_mono, ∫ g⁻(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ_V ≤ μ_V(B_t(x)).toReal. Multiplying by t⁻¹^n ≥ 0 gives t⁻¹^n ∫ g⁻(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ_V ≤ b(t).
Hence a < b(t) for all t in a set belonging to 𝓝[>] 0.

5. Upper bound. Let 0 < κ < 1 and a ∈ ℝ with θ w κ^{-n} < a, where κ^{-n} := (κ⁻¹)^n. Put g⁺ := χ_{1,κ⁻¹}; note 1 < κ⁻¹.
- Pointwise g⁺ ≤ 1_{B_{κ⁻¹}(0)}, since g⁺ ≤ 1 and g⁺ = 0 when ‖y‖ > κ⁻¹. By 3(c),(d), I⁺ := ∫_{T.plane} g⁺ dH^n ≤ w κ^{-n}, so θ I⁺ < a.
- By (A) applied to g⁺, eventually t⁻¹^n ∫ g⁺(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ_V(z) < a.
- Take 0 < t < κδ; then t·κ⁻¹ ≤ δ. For every z, 1_{B_t(x)}(z) ≤ g⁺(t⁻¹ • (z − x)): if z ∈ B_t(x) then ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ ≤ 1, so g⁺ = 1; otherwise the indicator is 0 ≤ g⁺.
- By 3(a),(b) and integral_mono, b(t) ≤ t⁻¹^n ∫ g⁺(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ_V.
Hence b(t) < a eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.

6. b(t) → θ w as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. Use the order characterization of convergence in ℝ (tendsto_order).
- If a < θ w: the map κ ↦ θ w κ^n is continuous and equals θ w at κ = 1. So the set of κ with θ w κ^n > a is a neighbourhood of 1, and it contains some κ ∈ (0,1). Step 4 gives a < b(t) eventually.
- If a > θ w: the map κ ↦ θ w κ^{-n} is continuous at κ = 1 (κ ≠ 0) with value θ w. So some κ ∈ (0,1) has θ w κ^{-n} < a. Step 5 gives b(t) < a eventually.

7. Conversion to the density ratio. Let 0 < t < δ.
- μ_V(B_t(x)) ≤ μ_V(B_δ(x)) < ∞, so μ_V(B_t(x)) = ofReal(m_t) with m_t := μ_V(B_t(x)).toReal.
- ω · ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(w) · ofReal(t^n) = ofReal(w t^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_mul).
- Since w t^n > 0, densityRatio n μ_V x t = ofReal(m_t)/ofReal(w t^n) = ofReal(m_t/(w t^n)) (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos) = ofReal(b(t)/w), because m_t/(w t^n) = t⁻¹^n m_t / w.
By step 6, b(t)/w → θ w / w = θ. Since ofReal is continuous (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal), ofReal(b(t)/w) → ofReal θ. The functions densityRatio n μ_V x and t ↦ ofReal(b(t)/w) agree on (0, δ) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). So Tendsto.congr' gives densityRatio n μ_V x → ofReal θ along 𝓝[>] 0, i.e. HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal θ). ∎

subproblems.title: μ-null sets of positive upper n-density are H^n-null (via Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.3)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^N (Borel σ-algebra), and U ⊆ ℝ^N open with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let Z ⊆ U be an arbitrary set (not necessarily measurable) with μ(Z) = 0 (outer measure). Suppose limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ > 0 for every x ∈ Z, where densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(closedBall x ρ)/(unitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρ)^n) ∈ [0,∞] and the limsup is along 𝓝[>] 0. Then H^n(Z) = μHE[n](Z) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (U Z : Set (Euclidean N)), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K ≠ ∞) → Z ⊆ U → μ Z = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, 0 < limsup (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0)) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) Z = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, stated for a general locally finite μ. Two small changes from that proof:
- its compact exhaustion K_p of U is replaced by an equivalent countable cover of U by balls with compact closure in U;
- its threshold θ(x) ≥ 1/k is phrased as upper density ≥ 1/(k+1). At points of M the upper density equals θ(x), by step 3.
The key ingredient is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3: for Borel regular μ on a metric space and A₁ ⊆ A₂, if Θ*^n(μ, A₂, x) ≥ t on A₁ then t·H^n(A₁) ≤ μ(A₂).
Lean prerequisite: Submission.lean must add three imports: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.EuclideanHausdorffUpper and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLiteral. The comparator allows extra imports, and a lean4export comparison showed that these imports leave every Contract definition byte-identical.
Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n. realUnitBallVolume, dimensionalDensityQuotient, dimensionalUpperDensity and simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal are SimonGMT's Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01 notions.

1. Normalizations.
(a) ω = realUnitBallVolume n. If n > 0, apply Chapter01.volume_euclidean_ball_eq at x = 0, r = 1: volume(ball 0 1) = realUnitBallVolume n · ofReal(1)^n. If n = 0, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is a one-point space, so ball 0 1 = univ and volume = dirac 0 (volume_euclideanSpace_eq_dirac); hence ω = 1 = realUnitBallVolume 0 (realUnitBallVolume_zero).
(b) For every A ⊆ ℝ^N, simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n A = μHE[n] A. This follows from (simonHausdorffMeasureReal n).toOuterMeasure = simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure, valid since n ≥ 0) and simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = μHE[n] (Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure).
(c) Every Borel set is Carathéodory-measurable for the outer measure μ.toOuterMeasure (le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory μ, with BorelSpace.measurable_eq).

2. Countable cover by balls of finite mass. For each y ∈ U pick r_y > 0 with closedBall y r_y ⊆ U (U is open: take half the radius of an open ball around y inside U). Let W_y := ball y r_y. Then μ(W_y) ≤ μ(closedBall y r_y) < ∞, because closed balls of ℝ^N are compact. ℝ^N is second countable, so there is a countable C ⊆ U with ⋃_{y∈C} W_y = ⋃_{y∈U} W_y (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). Since y ∈ W_y, this union contains U ⊇ Z.

3. Level sets. For y ∈ C and k ∈ ℕ let Z_{y,k} := {x ∈ Z ∩ W_y : (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ}. Every x ∈ Z lies in some W_y with y ∈ C (step 2). Its limsup is ≠ 0, so there is k with k⁻¹ < limsup (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt), and (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ k⁻¹. Hence Z ⊆ ⋃_{y∈C} ⋃_{k∈ℕ} Z_{y,k}.

4. Small open neighbourhoods. Fix y ∈ C, k ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0, ∞].
- The measure ν := μ.restrict W_y has ν(ℝ^N) = μ(W_y) < ∞. So ν is a finite Borel measure on a metric space, hence outer regular (Mathlib instance for finite measures on pseudo-metrizable spaces).
- ν(Z_{y,k}) ≤ μ(Z_{y,k}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 < ε.
- By outer regularity, which holds for arbitrary sets (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt), there is an open O' ⊇ Z_{y,k} with ν(O') < ε.
Put O := O' ∩ W_y. Then O is open, Z_{y,k} ⊆ O (because Z_{y,k} ⊆ W_y), and μ(O) = ν(O') < ε (Measure.restrict_apply, O' being measurable).

5. Densities relative to O. Let x ∈ Z_{y,k}. O is open and contains x, so ball x η ⊆ O for some η > 0. For 0 < ρ < η, closedBall x ρ ⊆ ball x η ⊆ O, so μ(O ∩ closedBall x ρ) = μ(closedBall x ρ). By 1(a) and ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(ρ)^n (ENNReal.rpow_natCast), dimensionalDensityQuotient μ n O x ρ = μ(O ∩ closedBall x ρ)/(realUnitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρ)^n) equals densityRatio n μ x ρ for every ρ ∈ (0, η). That interval belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). Therefore (limsup_congr) dimensionalUpperDensity μ n O x = limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ ≥ (k+1)⁻¹.

6. Comparison theorem. Use Simon's Theorem 3.3 in the form Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity. It holds in any metric space, for any outer measure whose Carathéodory σ-algebra contains the Borel sets, with arbitrary sets A₁, A₂ and threshold t ∈ [0,∞]. Apply it to:
- the outer measure μ.toOuterMeasure (allowed by 1(c)) and real dimension n ≥ 0;
- A₁ := Z_{y,k}, A₂ := O and t := (k+1)⁻¹, with the density hypothesis from step 5.
This gives (k+1)⁻¹ · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (Z_{y,k}) ≤ μ(O). By 1(b) and step 4, (k+1)⁻¹ · μHE[n](Z_{y,k}) ≤ μ(O) < ε.

7. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, (k+1)⁻¹ · μHE[n](Z_{y,k}) = 0 (le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense). As k+1 ≠ ∞, (k+1)⁻¹ ≠ 0 (ENNReal.inv_ne_zero), so μHE[n](Z_{y,k}) = 0.

8. By step 3 and monotonicity, μHE[n](Z) ≤ μHE[n](⋃_{y∈C} ⋃_k Z_{y,k}). This is 0 by countable subadditivity over the countable index set C × ℕ (measure_biUnion_null_iff with C countable, then measure_iUnion_null_iff over k). ∎

Lean route: verified without sorry in a scratch copy, about 110 lines including the two normalization lemmas; axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: Normalizations: unitBallVolume n = realUnitBallVolume n; simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n = μHE[n] as outer measures; Borel sets are Carathéodory-measurable for μ.
Countably many balls W_y of finite μ-mass with compact closure in U cover Z; split Z into Z_{y,k} = Z ∩ W_y ∩ {upper density ≥ 1/(k+1)}.
Outer regularity of the finite measure μ⌞W_y gives an open O ⊇ Z_{y,k} with μ(O) < ε.
At points of Z_{y,k} ⊆ O (O open), Simon's upper density of μ relative to O equals limsup densityRatio n μ x ≥ 1/(k+1).
Simon 1.3.3 (mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity) gives (k+1)⁻¹ H^n(Z_{y,k}) ≤ μ(O) < ε, so H^n(Z_{y,k}) = 0.
Countable subadditivity gives H^n(Z) = 0.
